reading: One entry per selected pair. For unchanged growth after rounds 1 through 16, a member is older if it was born before the snapshot. Waiting in the next transition is read separately after rounds 1 through 15. A common class contains at least one strictly own live member of each end. At loss, its successors are classified by actual parentage, with an unchanged member its own successor. The class number is local to its snapshot. The census file does not supply class ages or sizes.
extent: All 293 archived second-pass selections under caps three to six; each baseline through round 16, its first addition through the first loss of a common class (at most round 10). The detailed control and first-addition pair are read through round 13. A complementary class split and its two one-knot controls are read through round 8.

detailed_trace.description: Three mutually sharing receiver knots, site with one loose distinction and the others two. The far three knots form a path, joined at the middle knot with one loose distinction, the ends with two each before the meeting.

split_and_rescue.description: Both starts have three mutually sharing knots. The receiver has loose counts 1,2,2 and the far end has 1,1,2. Both meet at the first one-loose knot.
split_and_rescue.local_comparison: With the extra offshoot after round 3, follow the unmatched child at each of the next three rounds. The round-7 child and the eventual short knot have a parent in common. This gives a fourth distinct partner to a knot with the same parent-derived name as a three-partner knot in the unchanged growth. The cap supplied three in both.
split_and_rescue.scope: The two extra supplies after round 7 are controls for the immediate loss of the link. They are placed at knots with mixed ancestry. The check ends in round 8.

agreement_with_archive: All 293 selected first additions match setting member, holder steps and first round where the linked reading ceases to be true.
